items.prompt:
Read the story.

Asha laid a checkered blanket on the grass, unpacked a basket of sandwiches, and poured lemonade into paper cups while her family found spots in the shade.

What is Asha's family doing?
A) Cleaning the house
B) Having a picnic
C) Going to school
D) Painting a fence

steps: The blanket on grass, basket of sandwiches, and lemonade are picnic items.
The family finds spots in the shade to eat outside.
So they are having a picnic, choice B.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Because the bridge was closed for repairs, Mr. Lee had to drive the long way around the lake, and he arrived at work half an hour late.

Why was Mr. Lee late?
A) He woke up late
B) His car broke down
C) The bridge was closed, so he drove the long way
D) He stopped for breakfast
items.answer: C) The bridge was closed, so he drove the long way

steps: The question asks why he was late.
The story says "the bridge was closed for repairs" so he "had to drive the long way."
That is the stated reason, choice C.
solution.answer: C) The bridge was closed, so he drove the long way

items.prompt:
Read the poem.

The kettle sings, the window steams,
A blanket waits on Grandpa's chair.
He stirs the cocoa, humming low,
While snowflakes tumble through the air.

What season does the poem describe?
A) Summer
B) Spring
C) Winter
D) A hot afternoon

steps: Look for clues about the weather.
The poem mentions cocoa, a blanket, a steamy window, and "snowflakes tumble through the air."
Snow and cocoa point to winter, choice C.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Rosa had never ridden the tall roller coaster before. In line, she gripped the railing and kept checking the exit gate, but when her cousin offered to sit beside her, Rosa took a deep breath and climbed in.

How does Rosa most likely feel while waiting in line?
A) Bored and sleepy
B) Nervous but willing to try
C) Angry at her cousin
D) Sure she will not ride
items.answer: B) Nervous but willing to try

steps: She grips the railing and checks the exit, showing nervousness.
But she takes a deep breath and "climbed in," so she still tries.
That combination is nervous but willing, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Nervous but willing to try

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The kitchen counter was dusted with flour, a mixing bowl sat in the sink, and a warm smell drifted from the oven. On the table cooled a tray of golden muffins, and a note read, "Save some for your brother."

What detail best shows that someone has recently been baking?
A) The note on the table
B) The brother is mentioned
C) A warm smell drifts from the oven and muffins cool on the table
D) The counter is made of wood
items.answer: C) A warm smell drifts from the oven and muffins cool on the table

steps: The question asks which detail shows recent baking.
Flour, a used bowl, a warm oven smell, and cooling muffins all point to baking.
The clearest baking evidence is the warm smell and cooling muffins, choice C.
solution.answer: C) A warm smell drifts from the oven and muffins cool on the table

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the new student could not find the right classroom, most kids just pointed down the hall. Theo closed his locker, walked her all the way to the door, and said, "I got lost my first day too."

What can you infer about Theo from his actions?
A) He is in a hurry
B) He is kind and remembers what it feels like to be new
C) He dislikes the new student
D) He is late for class
items.answer: B) He is kind and remembers what it feels like to be new

steps: Others only pointed, but Theo walked her to the door.
He says, "I got lost my first day too," showing understanding.
That shows kindness and empathy, choice B.
solution.answer: B) He is kind and remembers what it feels like to be new

items.prompt:
Read the story.

For weeks, Grandpa had promised to teach Mateo how to fix the old radio. Each evening after dinner, they took it apart piece by piece. Grandpa's hands shook now and he worked slowly, but he never let Mateo rush. On the night the radio finally crackled to life, Grandpa did not smile at the sound. He smiled at Mateo.

Why does Grandpa smile at Mateo instead of at the working radio?
A) The radio still did not work
B) He cared more about the time and skills he shared with Mateo than the radio itself
C) He was tired of the radio
D) He wanted Mateo to keep the radio
items.answer: B) He cared more about the time and skills he shared with Mateo than the radio itself

steps: Grandpa spent weeks patiently teaching Mateo, never rushing.
When the radio worked, he smiled "at Mateo," not at the radio.
That shows the shared time mattered more than the radio, choice B.
solution.answer: B) He cared more about the time and skills he shared with Mateo than the radio itself

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The island had one small store, and every winter it ran low on supplies before the supply boat could return. That year, when the shelves grew bare, the shopkeeper began leaving her door unlocked with a box marked "Take what you need, leave what you can." By spring, the box was fuller than it had started.

Which inference is best supported by the ending?
A) The islanders stole from the box
B) The islanders shared and gave back, so the community took care of one another
C) The supply boat never came
D) The shopkeeper lost money on the box
items.answer: B) The islanders shared and gave back, so the community took care of one another

steps: The box invited people to take and to leave what they could.
By spring the box was "fuller than it had started."
That means people gave back more than they took, showing shared care, choice B.
solution.answer: B) The islanders shared and gave back, so the community took care of one another
